Subject: Renewal pricing discussion: per-token smoothing & thresholds

Hi Aditya,

We're starting the renewal planning for ScaleApps and wanted to flag a key ask from the finance and infra teams: our month-to-month token usage is spiky (bots + seasonal campaigns) and the straight per-token tiers are causing significant month-end overages.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood offer a smoothing window or rolling average for per-token pricing so our effective rate doesn't spike based on single-month bursts?
- If smoothing isn't feasible, can we get a temporary soft-cap / grace band for usage spikes that rolls into a true-up? If so, what uplift or ceiling would Redwood require?

We can share a 12-month usage forecast and an example spike (attached). Our renewal is targeted for mid-December and we need contract language for a possible amendment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if that helps.

Best,
Ellie Zhang
Head of Infrastructure, ScaleApps

Hi Ellie — thanks for the note and for sharing the forecast. I read through the attachment; makes sense why you want a smoother monthly bill. We have three pragmatic ways we typically approach this that balance predictability for you and revenue protection for Redwood:

1) Rolling smoothing window (recommended): a 6-month rolling average for per-token effective rate. Usage above the rolling baseline is true-upped monthly but billed at a blended (smoothed) per-token rate.

2) Soft-cap + small uplift: allow a soft-cap (e.g., 10–20% above committed tier) for short spikes; if sustained, overage is charged at an uplifted rate. One-time spike credits can be negotiated for exceptional events.

3) Temporary committed tier increase: a short-term commitment bump (90 days) with stepped discounts that revert after the period.

I attached a brief note with example math and how the blended rate would look at different spike profiles. A few quick Qs so we can draft an amendment:
- Do you want smoothing applied to 6- or 12-month windows?
- Is a true-up monthly OK, or do you prefer quarterly?
- Any internal limits on acceptable uplift (e.g., procurement requires <=15% ceiling)?

If it helps, I can propose a concrete amendment for the 6-month rolling option with a 12% uplift ceiling as a starting point and loop in procurement for redlines. Available for a 30-min slot tomorrow 11am PT.

Regards,
Aditya Rao

Aditya / Karthik — distilling this into concrete scenarios for legal and finance. I'm pasting the recommended scenarios and high-level P&L impact (see attached CSV with line-level math):

Scenario A — 6-month rolling smoothing (recommended)- Mechanics: compute 6-month rolling average usage; bill overages monthly but at a blended per-token smoothed rate.
- Commercial: Add a 12% uplift ceiling applied to any blended overage pricing; 30% max discount ceiling overall (tiers unchanged).
- Rationale: preserves revenue profile while materially reducing customer MRR volatility. Low operational overhead.

Scenario B — 12-month smoothing (conservative)- Mechanics: same as A but 12-month window.
- Commercial: 10% uplift ceiling, stricter true-up cadence (quarterly).
- Rationale: best customer predictability; highest revenue risk if long tail spikes.

Scenario C — Temporary step-up commit- Mechanics: 90-day committed bump to next tier, with step-down credits if usage drops.
- Commercial: 18% temporary discount applied to bumped commit; requires signed amendment and baseline changes.
- Rationale: Simplest contract language; more gating from procurement.

Recommendation: present Scenario A to ScaleApps first. Approve the 12% uplift ceiling (aditya, can we keep as the askable maximum?) and authorize legal to draft an amendment with a 6-month rolling window and monthly true-up.

Operational notes: we will need to flag this as a billing-side change in the Console (billing route + smoothing flag) and add a short eval to ensure token accounting matches their reported metrics. I attached scenario_calcs.csv with modeled usage and revenue impact across the next 12 months.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Hi Ellie — thanks for the patience while we modeled options with finance and product. Based on your usage patterns and procurement feedback, here's the proposal Redwood recommends and is ready to put in an amendment:

Chosen approach (what we'll propose in the amendment)
- 6-month rolling smoothing window for per-token billing (monthly measurements).
- Monthly true-up for any usage above the rolling baseline, billed at a blended smoothed per-token rate.
- Uplift ceiling: 12% over the baseline per-token list rate for blended overage pricing (this is the maximum uplift we will apply).
- One-time spike credit: for a single month spike >25% vs baseline, Redwood will issue a partial credit (up to 50% of the uplift portion) to help absorb an unexpected event; credit to be applied once per contract year.
- Term: apply for the upcoming 12-month renewal term; allow one review at 6 months for operational adjustments.

Next steps
1) If this looks good, we will route an amendment (DocuSign) to ScaleApps legal. Link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc-ScaleApps-Amendment
2) Please confirm the smoothing window (we used 6 months above), true-up cadence (monthly), and whether procurement requires any specific billing contact.
3) Once signed, product will enable the smoothing flag on your billing route and finance will send a short confirmation of how blended rates will be shown on invoices.

If you want, we can run a quick 20-minute walkthrough of the amendment and the invoice example; propose Thursday 11am PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this and making billing less painful for you.

Best,
